title: Kissed Malaysian Chicken Satay
description: A refreshing Malaysian dish featuring tender chicken, a tangy cranberry sauce, and a delicate leaf wrap - perfect for a weekend brunch.
instructions: In a blender or food processor, combine lemongrass paste, galangal paste, coconut milk, cranberry juice, honey, and fish sauce (if using). Blend until smooth.
In a large pan, heat 1 tablespoon of oil over medium heat. Add the chicken breast and cook until browned on all sides and cooked through, about 5-7 minutes.
Transfer the chicken to a plate and set aside.
In the same pan, add the remaining 1 tablespoon of oil. Add the tofu and cook until golden brown, about 3-5 minutes.
Add the blended sauce to the pan and stir to combine. Bring the sauce to a simmer and cook for 2-3 minutes, until slightly thickened.
To assemble the satay, place a pandanus leaf on a flat surface. Arrange 2-3 pieces of the cooked chicken and tofu on the leaf, followed by a spoonful of the sauce.
Fold the pandanus leaf over the filling to form a neat package. Repeat with the remaining ingredients.
Serve the satay immediately, garnished with fresh cilantro or scallions if desired.
To steam the satay, place them in a steamer basket over boiling water, cover with a lid, and steam for 5-7 minutes, until the filling is heated through and the leaves are tender.
